python_igraph.notes: Rust port runs the karate fixture in ~71% of python-igraph's median wall time; on ring-of-cliques 4x5 the two are within noise of one another (Rust 115 µs vs python-igraph 128 µs).

notes: Hot loop is the Brandes unweighted edge-betweenness pass, executed once per edge removed (m iterations total). Per iteration is O(|V| * |E_active|), matching the C reference O(|V| * |E|^2) overall complexity.

Scratch buffers (sigma, dist, pred, stack, delta_v, eb_now, queue) are allocated once outside the removal loop and reused; the per-iteration cost is dominated by BFS hops + dependency-accumulation pushes, not allocation.

Edge removals are implemented by masking (per-endpoint Vec<EdgeId> with retain) rather than mutating the graph, so the original `EdgeId`s remain stable across the whole run and can be replayed by callers.
Dendrogram replay (stage 2) is O(merges * n) for the label rewrite + O(n) per modularity recompute, totalling O(n^2) — negligible next to the Brandes loop on every graph we benchmark here.
